{"path":"snake_anthropic-claude-sonnet-5_01.html","edit_description":"
Create a complete, self-contained classic Snake game in a single HTML file (inline CSS in <style>, inline JS in <script>, no external dependencies). Requirements:

GRID & CORE MECHANICS
- 30x30 grid rendered on an HTML <canvas> (e.g. 600x600px, 20px cells), centered on page with dark theme styling.
- Snake(s) move continuously in one of four directions (up/down/left/right) at a fixed tick interval (e.g. 120ms, using setInterval/requestAnimationFrame with accumulator).
- Snake cannot instantly reverse into itself (e.g. if moving right, pressing left is ignored while there's more than 1 segment).
- Eating food grows the snake by one segment and increases that player's score by 1; a new food tile spawns randomly on an empty cell.
- Collision with a wall (grid boundary) or with own body or with the other snake's body (in two-snake modes) ends the game for that snake.
- Game ends fully when any snake dies; declare winner/loser/draw appropriately when two snakes are in play.

GAME MODES (selectable from start menu)
1. Human vs Human: two snakes controlled by two players on the same keyboard.
   - Player 1: Arrow keys (Up/Down/Left/Right)
   - Player 2: WASD keys
2. CPU vs Human: one snake controlled by keyboard (Arrow keys), one snake controlled by simple AI.
3. CPU vs CPU: both snakes controlled by AI (for a hands-off demo/spectate mode).
- Also support a simple single-snake "vs" note: if only one snake exists conceptually it's fine to always render two snakes for vs-modes, but make sure single relevant control scheme is used per mode (e.g. in CPU vs Human only Arrow keys matter, in Human vs Human both Arrow keys and WASD matter).

CPU AI
- Implement a reasonably good deterministic AI: on each tick, evaluate the 4 possible next moves (excluding immediate reverse), filter moves that would cause immediate wall/self/other-snake collision, and pick the move that greedily minimizes Manhattan (or BFS-based) distance to the current food tile. If no safe move reduces distance, pick any safe move (avoid death). If no safe move exists at all, allow the snake to move into a losing collision (game over triggers naturally).
- Keep the AI code compact but effective; a simple greedy/heuristic approach is sufficient (BFS for shortest path is a nice-to-have but not mandatory).

UI / SCREENS
- Start Menu screen (shown on load): title "Snake", buttons or number-key selectable options for the three modes (1 = Human vs Human, 2 = CPU vs Human, 3 = CPU vs CPU), and a "Press Enter or click to start" hint. Style with clean centered layout, dark background, readable fonts.
- In-game HUD: display live score(s) during gameplay — for two-snake modes show "Player 1 (or CPU 1): X" and "Player 2 (or CPU 2): Y" scores at the top of the canvas area. Distinguish snake colors (e.g. green vs orange/blue) with a small legend.
- Game Over screen: shown when the game ends, displaying final score(s), a message indicating winner/loser/draw (for two-snake modes) and instruction "Press Enter/Space to restart" or "Press M for menu".
- Keyboard-driven flow: on start menu, number keys 1/2/3 select mode and Enter/Space starts; on game over screen, Enter or Space restarts the same mode, and Escape or M returns to the start menu. All of this must also work via on-screen clickable buttons as a convenience, but keyboard restart is mandatory per the spec.

CODE STRUCTURE
- Single file, valid HTML5 document with <!DOCTYPE html>, all CSS inside a single <style> tag in <head>, all JS inside a single <script> tag before </body> (or at the end of body), no external libraries/CDNs, no build step — must run by simply opening the file in a browser.
- Use a clean game-state machine: STATE_MENU, STATE_PLAYING, STATE_GAMEOVER, with a single main loop that renders based on current state.
- Use requestAnimationFrame for the render/input loop and a separate fixed-timestep tick for snake movement logic so controls feel responsive while movement stays grid-locked.
- Add concise comments explaining key sections (state machine, AI logic, collision detection, rendering).
- Make sure keydown default behavior (page scrolling on arrow keys/space) is prevented via event.preventDefault() where relevant.

Deliver fully working, polished code — this is the final artifact, not a draft.
"}
